risk_semantics.annual: single initiating event under current weather; not weather-integrated total annual IR
risk_semantics.initiation: constant supplied hazard; disjoint first-event intervals; remaining consequence horizon; interval-left consequence approximation
risk_semantics.effect_combination: Frechet union upper bound min(1,sum(harm)) within one event branch; no independence assumed

limitations: If resolved gas equipment input is selected: the direct atmospheric plane is limited to Mach <=0.3; a higher-speed case requires a provider-resolved compressible_plane_handoff with a conservation-closed carrier section. PH/continuity/static enthalpy are checked, while provider kinetic-energy closure remains unqualified.

If resolved liquid/two-phase equipment input is selected: provider flash, gas/ground partition and total enthalpy are consumed; airborne liquid and provider flash/droplet physics remain outside this route.
Outdoor flat ground, non-calm wind, horizontal nozzle or provider-resolved vertical handoff, known leak geometry only.
A vertical provider exit is accepted only with a declared horizontal handoff section; the handoff is operator-limited and is not a PRISM rotation or independent vertical-jet validation.
A compressible/underexpanded gas handoff is consumed only at the provider-declared plane; PRISM does not expand, rotate or invent that plane from outlet pressure and velocity.
Ground deposition uses resolved per-class flight delays; distributed in-flight vapour generation is still collapsed to the terminal gas boundary at release time.

When a provider packet uses ParaHydrogen, the native DynamicLH2PoolX Hydrogen backend is reached only through the explicit declared pool fluid translation; the translation is operator-limited and does not claim cross-basis validation.
The gas branch enters a gas-only vector/cryogenic transition; nozzle vertical momentum is represented in fire geometry but not in this transition.
Rainout footprint is explicitly declared; it is not inferred from a single impact point or fitted to LFL/sensors.
Finite-volume top-hat reconstruction of native section averages; not the frozen seven-test FFI observation operator or independent transient validation.

If a sub-millisecond finite-release puff handoff violates SLABx monotonicity, PRISM first retries the same provider-resolved handoff as a finite-clock native puff; only if that backend retry fails does it use an instantaneous packet. The selected method, original error, finite retry error and temporal-shape preservation are recorded in dispersion_handoff_fallbacks.
Superposed carrier packets preserve H2 mass but overlapping air/temperature/pressure equilibration remains open.
Ignition probabilities, burn-back duration, radiation range and obstruction fraction are declared scenario inputs.
Fire does not feed heat back into the unignited pool evaporation model; ground flame deflection is a geometric approximation.
Quasi-steady flame geometry is used for short releases; flame establishment and propagation are unresolved.
Radiation uses the explicitly supplied fraction range; unexplained legacy Molina factor 22.7 is not used.
Blast uses two TNO anchor zones, not a continuous pressure/impulse curve; detonation and DDT unsupported.
Gas outside the configured spatial domain is explicitly ledgered; its flammable contribution and blast harm are uncomputed.
Hydrogen source mass accounting closes; total source-to-cloud energy closure and facility calibration are unqualified.
Numerical connection and timing measurements do not establish IJHE validation or 1-Hz fresh-physics capability.

consequence.limitation: Executable complete diagnostic chain within declared assumptions; engineering/facility validation remains withheld.

limitations: If resolved gas equipment input is selected: the direct atmospheric plane is limited to Mach <=0.3; a higher-speed case requires a provider-resolved compressible_plane_handoff with a conservation-closed carrier section. PH/continuity/static enthalpy are checked, while provider kinetic-energy closure remains unqualified.

If resolved liquid/two-phase equipment input is selected: provider flash, gas/ground partition and total enthalpy are consumed; airborne liquid and provider flash/droplet physics remain outside this route.
Outdoor flat ground, non-calm wind, horizontal nozzle or provider-resolved vertical handoff, known leak geometry only.
A vertical provider exit is accepted only with a declared horizontal handoff section; the handoff is operator-limited and is not a PRISM rotation or independent vertical-jet validation.
A compressible/underexpanded gas handoff is consumed only at the provider-declared plane; PRISM does not expand, rotate or invent that plane from outlet pressure and velocity.
Ground deposition uses resolved per-class flight delays; distributed in-flight vapour generation is still collapsed to the terminal gas boundary at release time.

When a provider packet uses ParaHydrogen, the native DynamicLH2PoolX Hydrogen backend is reached only through the explicit declared pool fluid translation; the translation is operator-limited and does not claim cross-basis validation.
The gas branch enters a gas-only vector/cryogenic transition; nozzle vertical momentum is represented in fire geometry but not in this transition.
Rainout footprint is explicitly declared; it is not inferred from a single impact point or fitted to LFL/sensors.
Finite-volume top-hat reconstruction of native section averages; not the frozen seven-test FFI observation operator or independent transient validation.

If a sub-millisecond finite-release puff handoff violates SLABx monotonicity, PRISM first retries the same provider-resolved handoff as a finite-clock native puff; only if that backend retry fails does it use an instantaneous packet. The selected method, original error, finite retry error and temporal-shape preservation are recorded in dispersion_handoff_fallbacks.
Superposed carrier packets preserve H2 mass but overlapping air/temperature/pressure equilibration remains open.
Ignition probabilities, burn-back duration, radiation range and obstruction fraction are declared scenario inputs.
Fire does not feed heat back into the unignited pool evaporation model; ground flame deflection is a geometric approximation.
Quasi-steady flame geometry is used for short releases; flame establishment and propagation are unresolved.
Radiation uses the explicitly supplied fraction range; unexplained legacy Molina factor 22.7 is not used.
Blast uses two TNO anchor zones, not a continuous pressure/impulse curve; detonation and DDT unsupported.
Gas outside the configured spatial domain is explicitly ledgered; its flammable contribution and blast harm are uncomputed.
Hydrogen source mass accounting closes; total source-to-cloud energy closure and facility calibration are unqualified.
Numerical connection and timing measurements do not establish IJHE validation or 1-Hz fresh-physics capability.

semantics.risk_sum: validated risk atoms are summed once across disjoint equipment campaigns
semantics.missing_scope: missing or incomplete equipment/families remain partial and never become zero risk
semantics.frequency: each atom retains its initiating event frequency; no frequency inference or reallocation is performed
semantics.frequency_port_binding: reviewed event port_ids are carried into cases and risk_atoms and checked again at facility merge; missing or mismatched port rows withhold the facility scope
semantics.provider_packet: qualified provider packet evidence is counted separately from the numerical risk sum; a provider release history never creates or changes an initiating frequency
semantics.fn: expected-death F-N curves use the same atom-level convention as the campaign backend
semantics.conditional_diagnostic_facility: facility IR/F-N is calculated from the atoms that reached the risk ledger, but remains diagnostic-only whenever declared scope, physical validation, or release-horizon blockers are present
semantics.timing: whole-case and per-stage elapsed milliseconds are observed execution evidence; they are not repeated-run latency, throughput, or a fresh-physics 1 Hz claim
semantics.component_coverage: each case is assigned to its provider component when available, then to its event component; conditional case identities are deduplicated, while strict uncomputed counts retain raw evidence rows and never create a frequency
semantics.scenario_family_contributions: risk atoms retain their declared scenario_families; overlapping physical families are views of the same atoms and must not be summed across families
semantics.component_risk_ranking: equipment rows are ranked by peak receptor IR from the same conditional risk atoms; this is a diagnostic triage view and never reallocates frequency or promotes facility IR/F-N
semantics.scenario_branch_accounting: annual-condition weather, release/termination, and ignition branches are preserved as diagnostics over the same risk atoms; no branch frequency is inferred, reallocated, or double-counted
semantics.release_termination_inventory: case-level provider duration, termination, isolation, inventory and mass closure are retained in one facility ledger; withheld copies remain in the summary and are never converted to zero risk
